newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bonds end mixed, curve flattens.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bonds end mixed, curve flattens.

text.p: 1415 GMT - The trend of a flattening Swedish bond curve continued on Thursday as yields ended mixed with the long end of the market falling somewhat while the shorter end rose on worries about inflation picking up.
The worries were triggered by statistics last week showing a higher than expected CPI figure for June, up 0.1 percent from May instead of an expected fall of 0.1 percent.

The crown was little changed against the mark. * Six-month T-bill rate rises four basis points to 4.29 pct * Ten-year bond yield falls two basis points to 6.39 pct * Crown flat at 4.2885 to mark vs 4.2815 late on Wednesday

The trend of a flattening Swedish bond curve continued on Thursday as yields ended mixed with the long end of the market falling somewhat while the shorter end rose on worries about inflation picking up.
Concern was triggered by statistics last week showing a higher than expected CPI figure for June, up 0.1 percent from May instead of an expected fall of 0.1 percent.
The six-month T-bill rate rose four basis points to 4.29 percent while the ten-year bond yield fell two to 6.39 pct
Dealers expected the flattening of the curve to cease in the short term.
"In the mid-term the flattening could continue. It depends on if we see more signs of rising inflation which makes shorter maturities less interesting compared to long maturities," a trader said.
Market players will keenly watch PPI figures for June, due to be released at 0800 GMT on Friday. Expectations target a 0.3 percent increase from May for an annualised 1.9 percent rise.
The crown was little changed at 4.2885 against the mark compared to 4.2815 late on Wednesday. But the crown softened to 7.8699 against the dollar from 7.8260.
